title: Continuous sections of a topological module sequence with finite discrete quotient
statement:
Let $A,T_0,T_1,T_2$ be commutative topological rings, with continuous unital homomorphisms $A\to T_i$ giving their $A$-module structures. Let $f:T_0\to T_1$ and $g:T_1\to T_2$ be continuous $A$-linear maps. Suppose $f$ is injective, $g$ is surjective, $\operatorname{im}f=\ker g$, $T_2$ is finite and discrete, and the induced bijection $T_0\to\ker g$ is a homeomorphism for the subspace topology on $\ker g$. For every profinite set $S$, the sequence of pointwise $C(S,A)$-modules
$$0\to C(S,T_0)\xrightarrow{f\circ-}C(S,T_1)\xrightarrow{g\circ-}C(S,T_2)\to0$$
is short exact. The postcomposition maps consequently give a short exact sequence of condensed $\underline A$-module objects $0\to\underline{T_0}\to\underline{T_1}\to\underline{T_2}\to0$, using the continuous-function sheaves of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

source.place: On the point: continuous division through the topological kernel and lifting the finite discrete values; Triangles: the same argument for quotient powers. General topological-module formulation of that argument.

proof.text: Fix a profinite set $S$. Write $\alpha_i:A\to T_i$ for the given continuous ring maps. Addition and scalar multiplication on $C(S,T_i)$ are pointwise: $(a\cdot u)(s)=\alpha_i(a(s))u(s)$. These functions are continuous by continuity of $\alpha_i$, addition and multiplication; the module axioms hold at every $s$. Define $F_S(u)=f\circ u$ and $G_S(v)=g\circ v$. Continuity follows by composition, and $A$-linearity pointwise gives $F_S(a\cdot u)(s)=\alpha_1(a(s))f(u(s))$ and $G_S(a\cdot v)(s)=\alpha_2(a(s))g(v(s))$. Thus both are $C(S,A)$-linear.

source.place: On the point: the pointwise module sequence

proof.text: If $F_S(u)=F_S(v)$, then $f(u(s))=f(v(s))$ for every $s$, so injectivity of $f$ gives $u=v$. Moreover $g(f(t))=0$ for every $t\in T_0$, since $\operatorname{im}f=\ker g$. Hence $G_SF_S=0$ and $\operatorname{im}F_S\subseteq\ker G_S$.

source.place: On the point: injectivity and the zero composite

proof.text: Let $v\in C(S,T_1)$ satisfy $G_S(v)=0$. Its values lie in $K=\ker g$. The map $\bar v:S\to K$ with the same values is continuous for the subspace topology: the inverse image of $K\cap U$ is $v^{-1}(U)$ for every open $U\subseteq T_1$. By hypothesis $h:T_0\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, $t\mapsto f(t)$, is a homeomorphism. Therefore $u=h^{-1}\circ\bar v$ is continuous and $F_S(u)=v$. Combined with step 2, this proves $\operatorname{im}F_S=\ker G_S$.

source.place: On the point: continuous division through the topological kernel

proof.text: For each $b\in T_2$ choose $t_b\in T_1$ with $g(t_b)=b$, using surjectivity of $g$. Given $w\in C(S,T_2)$, define $v(s)=t_{w(s)}$. For an open $U\subseteq T_1$ one has $v^{-1}(U)=\bigcup_{b:t_b\in U}w^{-1}(\{b\})$, an open set since $T_2$ is discrete. Thus $v$ is continuous and $G_S(v)=w$. This proves surjectivity and completes the short exact sequence on sections. The choices $t_b$ need not define a linear map; only the lift of each individual section is required.

source.place: On the point: lifting the finitely many values of the quotient

proof.text: Use [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] for the sheaves $\underline A$ and $\underline{T_i}$ on the coherent profinite site. The pointwise actions from step 1 commute with restriction, since $(a\cdot u)\circ q=(a\circ q)\cdot(u\circ q)$; postcomposition with $f,g$ also commutes with restriction. Thus these are sheaves of modules over the section-ring sheaf $\underline A$, with the morphisms of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Fix a universe of profinite sets and a larger coefficient universe so the site is essentially small as in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The monoidality and existence of abelian sheafification, including stability of its local equivalences under tensor, are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed]. Apply [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] to the commutative ring object $\underline A$. It identifies these module sheaves and their sectionwise morphisms with the module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], leaving sections and restrictions unchanged.

source.place: On the point: identifying continuous-function sheaves as condensed module objects

proof.text: In sectionwise module sheaves, [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] computes kernels sectionwise and cokernels by sheafifying sectionwise cokernels. Steps 2 and 3 therefore identify the kernel of the second arrow with the first sheaf, through its specified injective arrow. Step 4 makes the sectionwise cokernel of the second arrow zero, so its sheaf cokernel is zero. This proves short exactness of the module sheaf sequence. Under [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] it is exactly the claimed sequence of condensed $\underline A$-module objects: an equivalence transports the kernel and cokernel universal properties because it gives bijections on morphisms and every object is isomorphic to one in its image. Hence the transported sequence is short exact.

source.place: On the point: the concluding condensed-module short exactness

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N5-e0aea6a2d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full; the delivery adds no new nodes. The statement is unchanged and correctly generalizes the 'On the point' paragraph of sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution.proof.md (lines 5-13), which 'Triangles' (lines 24-31) reuses: injectivity, continuous division through the topological kernel, and lifting the values of the finite discrete quotient. Steps 1-4 are elementary and correct. The homeomorphism onto ker g is used only in step 3, and it is necessary: discrete Z_p mapping to p-adic Z_p with T2=0 fails without it. Discreteness of T2 is used in step 4. I read the statements of all six cited nodes. Step 5 matches them: sheaves of continuous functions; lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed supplies the hypothesis of def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence, which preserves sections and restrictions; and with a larger coefficient universe the site is essentially small. Step 6 uses the sectionwise kernel and the sheafified cokernel from def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, then transports across the equivalence. Both citations in the parent det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution meet every hypothesis: T2 is O_E/a^r with a^rA open, or the finite quotients B_m, B_{n+m}, B_n. Edge cases checked: S empty, S a point, T2=0. I found no duplicate in the DAG and no cycle. Mathlib was searched with all four tools.
